name: How does the Denver climate affect tile and marble installations?

mainEntity.name: How does the Denver climate affect tile and marble installations?

acceptedAnswer.text: In the greater Denver metro area, indoor humidity levels drop significantly in winter and rise in summer, causing wood subfloors and framing to expand and contract. For tile and marble installations, managing this seasonal movement is critical to prevent sheared tiles and crumbling grout. Installers often incorporate uncoupling membranes over wood substrates to isolate the tile assembly from subfloor shifting. Proper perimeter expansion gaps are also essential along baseboards, and mortar must be mixed and cured within controlled indoor temperatures to prevent dry winter air from leaching moisture out of thinset prematurely.
acceptedAnswer.description: Denver's dry climate and seasonal humidity swings cause subfloor movement, making uncoupling membranes and perimeter expansion gaps essential to prevent cracks.
